text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where code changes are automatically built and tested several times a day. When a developer pushes new code to a shared repository, a CI pipeline starts immediately. This pipeline runs automated builds to compile the software and then executes a suite of tests, including unit and integration tests. The main benefit is catching issues early, before they become bigger problems. If a test fails, the team is alerted right away, so they can fix the error quickly. This approach keeps the software stable, reduces manual work, and helps teams collaborate more effectively.
